title: World Cuisines & Signature Dishes
description: 36 original culinary questions on iconic dishes, spices, street foods, and gastronomic origins around the globe.
author: QuizRooms

questions.prompt: Which country is the birthplace of sushi, ramen, and tempura?
questions.explanation: Modern nigiri sushi developed in Edo (Tokyo) in the 19th century.

questions.prompt: Which Spanish rice dish from Valencia is traditionally cooked in a wide shallow pan with saffron?
questions.explanation: Traditional Valencian paella uses short-grain bomba rice, saffron, and a crispy bottom layer called socarrat.

questions.prompt: Which Egyptian national street-food dish layers rice, lentils, macaroni, chickpeas, crispy onions, and spiced tomato sauce?
questions.explanation: Koshary is Egypt's beloved hearty vegan comfort dish.

questions.prompt: Which spice, harvested from the stigmas of Crocus sativus flowers, is the world's most expensive spice by weight?
questions.explanation: Over 150,000 crocus flowers are needed to harvest just one kilogram of saffron.

questions.prompt: Which Italian city is recognized as the birthplace of modern Pizza Margherita?
questions.explanation: Neapolitan pizza making is listed by UNESCO as Intangible Cultural Heritage.

questions.prompt: Which fermented napa cabbage and radish side dish is a staple of Korean cuisine?
questions.explanation: Korea has hundreds of regional varieties of kimchi.

questions.prompt: Which fragrant Vietnamese noodle soup features a slow-simmered spiced beef or chicken broth?
questions.explanation: Pho originated in northern Vietnam in the early 20th century.

questions.prompt: Which classic Middle Eastern dip is made primarily from mashed chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, and garlic?
questions.explanation: Hummus is enjoyed across the Levant and Egypt with warm pita bread.

questions.prompt: Which Mexican dip is made from mashed ripe avocados, lime juice, cilantro, and salt?
questions.explanation: The word guacamole comes from the Nahuatl word 'āhuacamolli' (avocado sauce).

questions.prompt: Which traditional Moroccan slow-cooked stew is named after the conical earthenware pot in which it is cooked?
questions.explanation: The conical lid traps steam and returns moisture to the dish.

questions.prompt: Which French pastry is famous for its flaky crescent shape made with laminated butter dough?
questions.explanation: Although iconic in France, its ancestor was the Austrian kipferl.

questions.prompt: Which Thai stir-fried rice noodle dish combines tamarind, fish sauce, peanuts, egg, and bean sprouts?
questions.explanation: Pad Thai became Thailand's signature street food in the mid-20th century.

questions.prompt: Which traditional Jordanian and Palestinian dish features lamb cooked in fermented dried yogurt (jameed) served over rice?
questions.explanation: Mansaf is Jordan's national dish and a symbol of hospitality.

questions.prompt: Which fragrant spiced rice dish is considered a national staple of Saudi Arabia and the Arabian Gulf?
questions.explanation: Kabsa is flavored with black lime (loomi), cardamom, cloves, and cinnamon.

questions.prompt: Which beloved West African one-pot tomato-spiced rice dish sparks friendly culinary rivalry between Nigeria, Ghana, and Senegal?
questions.explanation: Jollof rice traces its roots to the Wolof people of Senegal and The Gambia.

questions.prompt: Which traditional Peruvian dish cures fresh raw fish in citrus juice (lime) with chili and red onion?
questions.explanation: The citric acid denatures the fish proteins without heat.

questions.prompt: Which Italian dessert layers espresso-soaked ladyfingers with mascarpone cream and cocoa powder?
questions.explanation: Tiramisu literally translates to 'pick me up' in Italian.

questions.prompt: Which Georgian boat-shaped cheese bread is traditionally topped with a runny egg yolk and butter?
questions.explanation: Adjarian khachapuri is Georgia's most famous culinary export.

questions.prompt: Which Ethiopian spongy sourdough flatbread made from teff flour serves as both plate and utensil?
questions.explanation: Diners tear off pieces of injera to scoop up spicy stews called wats.

questions.prompt: Which Canadian comfort dish tops French fries with cheese curds and hot brown gravy?
questions.explanation: Poutine originated in rural Quebec in the late 1950s.

questions.prompt: Which smoky Levantine dip is made from roasted eggplant blended with tahini, lemon, and olive oil?
questions.explanation: Charring the eggplant over an open flame gives it its signature smoky aroma.

questions.prompt: Which crispy pastry filled with spiced potatoes or meat is an iconic snack across India and South Asia?
questions.explanation: Samosas traveled along medieval trade routes from Central Asia and the Middle East to India.

questions.prompt: Which creamy Greek yogurt dip is mixed with grated cucumber, garlic, dill, and olive oil?
questions.explanation: Tzatziki is a classic pairing for gyros and souvlaki.

questions.prompt: Which Hungarian stew is richly seasoned with sweet paprika and slow-simmered beef?
questions.explanation: Goulash originated as a hearty meal cooked by Hungarian herdsmen (gulyás).

questions.prompt: Which crisp, spun shredded phyllo pastry dessert soaked in sweet syrup and filled with melted cheese or cream is famous in Nablus and across the Levant?
questions.explanation: Nabulsi knafeh uses white brine cheese and orange-blossom sugar syrup.

questions.prompt: Which traditional Argentine and Uruguayan green herb sauce is made with parsley, garlic, oregano, and vinegar for grilled meats?
questions.explanation: Chimichurri is essential at an Argentine asado barbecue.

questions.prompt: Which fiery Tunisian chili pepper paste is seasoned with caraway, coriander, and garlic?
questions.explanation: Tunisian harissa was added to UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2022.

questions.prompt: Which Belgian dish pairs steamed mussels with crispy twice-fried potatoes?
questions.explanation: Moules-frites is widely considered Belgium's national dish.

questions.prompt: Which South Indian thin crispy fermented crepe is made from rice and black lentil batter?
questions.explanation: Dosa is typically served with coconut chutney and sambar lentil stew.

questions.prompt: Which Japanese fermented soybean paste is the base of a classic savory soup?
questions.explanation: Miso comes in white (shiro), red (aka), and mixed varieties depending on fermentation time.

questions.prompt: Which Turkish and Levantine spice blend typically combines dried thyme/oregano, roasted sesame seeds, and tangy sumac?
questions.explanation: Za'atar is mixed with olive oil and baked onto flatbread (manakish).

questions.prompt: Which Italian northern rice dish is slowly stirred with warm broth until creamy?
questions.explanation: Arborio and Carnaroli are prized rice varieties for risotto.

questions.prompt: Which Polish filled dumplings can be stuffed with potato and cheese, sauerkraut, or sweet berries?
questions.explanation: Pierogi are a centerpiece of Polish home cooking and holiday tables.

questions.prompt: Which fragrant Southeast Asian coconut noodle soup is famous in Malaysia and Singapore?
questions.explanation: Laksa combines Chinese noodles with Southeast Asian coconut, lemongrass, and chili.

questions.prompt: Which classic British dish consists of battered fried white fish served with thick-cut chips and mushy peas?
questions.explanation: Fish and chips shops first appeared in England in the 1860s.

questions.prompt: Which famous dark Mexican sauce can contain over 20 ingredients including chilies, nuts, spices, and unsweetened chocolate?
questions.explanation: Mole poblano is celebrated as a culinary symbol of Puebla and Oaxaca.
